label: prf:toffoli-transfer-matrix
title: Proof of toffoli transfer matrix
html:
Proof. Proof of toffoli transfer matrix

Proof. On 3 strands, the chain reduction (transfer matrix product) produces two generators \sigma_0, \sigma_1 with traced volumes \hat{V}_0(q), \hat{V}_1(q).

Single-crossing type-blindness (key lemma). Generator \sigma_1 contains one crossing (strand 1 with strand 2). The traced volume is \hat{V}_1 = z \cdot c + d, where (c, d) depends on the crossing type. Direct computation yields:

  \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{pp})} = z \cdot 1 + 0 = z
  \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{mix})}
  = z \cdot 1 - \tfrac{q - q^{-1}}{2}
  = z - \tfrac{q - q^{-1}}{2}
  \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{nn})}
  = z \cdot 1 - (q - q^{-1})
  = z - (q - q^{-1})

These three values are not equal. They differ in the d coefficient. A single crossing therefore carries type information: \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{mix})} - \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{pp})} = -\tfrac{q - q^{-1}}{2} and \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{nn})} - \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{pp})} = -(q - q^{-1}).

What vanishes is the target-flip difference, not the type dependence. Generator \sigma_1 operates on strands 1 and 2. This is the control–control crossing. A target-flip acts on strand 3, leaving strands 1 and 2 unchanged. Parent and daughter therefore carry the same \sigma_1 crossing type, hence the same \hat{V}_1. This forces:

  \Delta_1 = \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{par})} - \hat{V}_1^{(\mathrm{dau})} = 0

for every target-flip transition. This occurs because the control crossing is fixed, not because \hat{V}_1 is type-independent.

Target-flip amplitude. Since \Delta_1 = 0, the 1-jet formula reduces to:

  P_{\mathrm{flip}} = \hat{V}_1 \cdot \Delta_0
  = z \cdot \bigl(\hat{V}_0^{(\mathrm{par})} -
    \hat{V}_0^{(\mathrm{dau})}\bigr)

The chain at \sigma_0 contains two crossings: (0,1) and (0,2). The target flip changes the (0,2) crossing type but leaves the (0,1) crossing unchanged. Chain reduction gives \hat{V}_0 = z \cdot a_0 + b_0, where a_0, b_0 depend on both crossings. The difference \Delta_0 factors. The unchanged (0,1) crossing contributes its coefficient c_{01} as a prefactor. The changing (0,2) crossing contributes the same core difference regardless of the (0,1) type.

Therefore P_{\mathrm{flip}} = c_{01} \cdot \Delta_{02}(q), where c_{01} is the crossing coefficient of the control–control pair and \Delta_{02} is the core difference at the changing crossing. Open (2026-08-30). This step used to name that core difference \Phi(q) and call it universal. The identification is withdrawn: \Phi is not in the image of the construction under any indexing or convention, and the derived flip amplitude is P_{7,6}(q) = -(q-1)(q+1)(q^6+q^4+2q^2+1)/2q(q^2+1)^2 under the canonical convention D. The factorisation itself — a prefactor from the unchanged crossing times a common core from the changing one — is what the argument above establishes and is unaffected; only the closed form assigned to the core is retired.

The S_3 orbit. The three choices of target strand in the ordering [\mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{n}] give:

Target Control pair c Amplitude
strand 2 \mathfrak{p}\mathfrak{p} 1 \Phi
strand 1 \mathfrak{p}\mathfrak{n} 1 \Phi
strand 0 \mathfrak{p}\mathfrak{n} 1 \Phi

The Toffoli selects the governor: the target with c = 1 (unit weight). In the (1, -(q - q^{-1})) convention, all crossing types share c = 1. The distinction moves to the d coefficient.

Antisymmetry. The reverse transition swaps parent and daughter, negating \Delta_0. Hence, P_{6,7} = -P_{7,6}.

Classical limit. At q = 1, q - q^{-1} = 0. All crossing types coincide, giving \Delta_0 = 0. The factor (q - 1) in \Phi confirms this.

Golden ratio zero of P_{7,7}. The numerator q + q^{1/2} - 1 vanishes when q^{1/2} = (\sqrt{5} - 1)/2 = 1/\varphi. This gives q = 1/\varphi^2 = (3 - \sqrt{5})/2. \square
